text:
Adam Fox is having the kind of season that usually ends with a trip to the awards show, and the scoring line is underselling it. He has 26 points in 23 games, 24 of them assists, while playing nearly 23 minutes a night. With him on the ice at five on five, the Rangers have taken almost 60% of the expected goals, the share of quality chances, 11 points better than when he sits. That's elite even by his standards.

The goals haven't followed the chances. New York has scored 5.4 fewer goals than its chances deserved with Fox on the ice, so if anything his point total is light. That usually swings back, and our projection puts him somewhere between 72 and 99 points by April.

Evolving-Hockey had him ninth among all defensemen in wins above replacement last season, with his team's chance creation with him on in the 99th percentile and the chances against shrinking too. Forever Blueshirts already has him in the trophy conversation. What to watch: whether the finishing catches up to the process, because when it does the numbers get loud.
